statement.p: An open box is to be made out of a 9-inch by 14-inch piece of cardboard by cutting out squares of equal size from the four corners and bending up the sides. If the box needs to be at least 1 inch deep, and no more than 3 inches deep, find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum volumes.

solution.p: You have a rectangle of size 9 by 14, and you cut a square out of each corner. Say each square has length x. Then when you fold the rectangle up, the height of the resulting box is x and the length is 14-2 x while the width is 9 -2 x. So the volume of the box is V=l \cdot w \cdot h = (14 -2 x) (9 -2 x)x= (126-46 x +4 x^2)x=126 x-46 x^2+4x^3 Taking the derivative and setting it equal to 0 gives V'=126-2\cdot 46 x+ 12x^2 =0 Using the quadratic formula, we get that x=\frac{2\cdot46\pm\sqrt{4\cdot46^2-4\cdot 12\cdot 126}}{2\cdot 12}= 1.7853 \mbox{ or } 5.88136762124075 But if x=5.88136762124075, then the width of the box, which is 9-2 x, is negative. So the height is x=1.7853.

Plugging back in, the length of the box is 14-2x=14-2\cdot1.7853=10.4294 and the width is 9-2x=9-2\cdot1.7853=5.4294 And so the volume at the local extremum is 10.4294 \cdot 5.4294 \cdot 1.7853 = 101.093.
We also calculate the volume at the endpoints, x=1 and x=3. (14-2)(9-2)\cdot 1 = 84, \mbox{ and } (14-6)(9-6)\cdot 3 = 72
So the absolute maximum of volume is 101.093 and the absolute minimum of volume is 72.
